full_judgment: 24. Now, with regard to the grievances made by the learned Advocate for the appellants that the defence case has not been considered by the learned Sessions Judge side by side with the prosecution case and this has resulted in a miscarriage of justice, let us see how far this is correct and tenable. In reply to the above grievance of the learned Advocate for the appellants, the learned DAG submits that the defence case as transpired from the cross-examination of the PWs and the statements of the appellant Shadat Ali at the time of his examination U/S 342 CrPC that deceased Akram Ali along with his brother Abdur Rahman and some witnesses trespassed into the house of Shahur and Shadat Ali and tried to abduct Shanu when Amena Khatun wife of Shadat Ali resisted and while resisting she also received some injuries on her person and on her cry neighbouring villagers rushed to the place of occurrence to the reseue of Amena Khatun and there was a commotion in which deceased Akram Ali and PW 3 Abdur Rahman sustained grievous injuries and nobody could identify the person or persons who caused the said injuries and further the occurrence did not take place at the time, place and in the manner as alleged by the prosecution. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the State that defence case has been duly considered by the trial Court and the above grievance on behalf of the appellants has no basis. In this connection, the learned DAG has drawn our attention to page 17 of the impugned judgment wherein it appears that the defence case has been duly considered by the trial Court. In urging this point of non-consideration of the defence case Mr. Faiz, the learned Advocate for the appellant has relied on some decisions reported in 38 DLR(AD) 311, 5 DLR FC 107 new page 64, 6 DLR (FC) 28 and 28 DLR 192 to show that if there is a defence case specially given, then the case of the prosecution as well as that of the defence has to be considered side by side and even if the defence fails to establish its case that will not make the prosecution case proved or established as the burden of proof on the prosecution never shifts. The prosecution in order to succeed must prove its own case beyond all reasonable doubt. This cardinal principle in the administration of criminal justice is well settled and we have nothing to differ with the same. We have only to see whether the grievance of non-consideration of the defence case is correct or not.
